title: A nonempty regular open ascends for separable fraction fields
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (an integral domain here means a nonzero commutative ring in which a product is zero only if one factor is zero) and let $R\to S$ be an injective ring homomorphism of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], with $S$ an integral domain. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $F=\operatorname{Frac}(S)$ be their fraction fields, namely fields consisting of fractions of elements of the indicated domains with nonzero denominator. Assume that the induced extension $F/K$ is separable in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. If $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] contains a nonempty open subset $U$ such that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every $\mathfrak p\in U$, then $\operatorname{Spec}S$ contains a nonempty open subset $V$ such that $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local for every $\mathfrak q\in V$.

source.place: Tag 07PB, lemma-J-0-goes-up; J-0 expanded using Tag 07P7, definition-J; separable field extension is Tag 030O, definition-separable-field-extension in algebra.tex.

proof.text: Choose p in U and a basic open D(f) containing p and contained in U, using the basic-open basis of [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then f is nonzero. Put A = R_f. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Every prime P of A contracts to p in D(f), since f is a unit in A. The localization of A at P is the localization of R at p by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] and [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Its regular localness follows from U. Thus A is regular by the ring clause of [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Tag 07PB, lemma-J-0-goes-up; J-0 expanded using Tag 07P7, definition-J; separable field extension is Tag 030O, definition-separable-field-extension in algebra.tex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-generic-smooth-domain] directly to the original map R to S and its given separable fraction-field embedding. Obtain g nonzero such that C = S_g is smooth over R. Set T = C_image(f). Then T is smooth over R by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization].

source.place: Tag 07PB, lemma-J-0-goes-up; J-0 expanded using Tag 07P7, definition-J; separable field extension is Tag 030O, definition-separable-field-extension in algebra.tex.

proof.text: The image of f is a unit in T, so the map from R factors through A. Formal smoothness over R implies formal smoothness over A: a lift of an R-algebra homomorphism necessarily respects the inverse of f, hence commutes with A. This is Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth.localization_base. Finite algebra generators over R remain generators over A by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Since A is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] gives finite presentation over A. By the formal-smoothness and finite-presentation characterization in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], T is smooth over A. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] to obtain regularity of T.

source.place: Tag 07PB, lemma-J-0-goes-up; J-0 expanded using Tag 07P7, definition-J; separable field extension is Tag 030O, definition-separable-field-extension in algebra.tex.

proof.text: Put a = image(f) times g, nonzero by injectivity and the domain hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization], T is a localization of S at powers of a (Mathlib IsLocalization.Away.mul). Take the basic open D(a), which contains the zero prime and hence is nonempty. Given q in D(a), powers of a avoid q. The extended prime Q in T contracts to q; localizing T at Q is also localization of S at q by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] and [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Uniqueness of localization supplies T_Q isomorphic to S_q. The former is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme] and regularity of T, hence so is the latter.
